supersedes: r79_roll/1 (configs/opencode_r79_roll.json is FROZEN and unaltered; the timestamp-stable clock + complete-validity changes are behavior-breaking vs r79 and live here)
version_choice: r80_roll/1 (not r79_roll/2): execution-bar indices change from first-seen counter order to timestamp-stable origin-anchored grid steps, and gap resolution changes from ANY-seen-inside to ALL-expected-valid-present. Both change economics on gapped feeds (the r79 counterexample divergence is the intended behavior change). A new major version prevents silent comparison of r79 vs r80 numbers on gapped data. Gapless in-order runs are bit-identical by construction (origin anchor reproduces 0..N-1).
policy_contract: FROZEN policy only (confirmed_dd_guard, v29-iso4 chain). No threshold/architecture/frequency/ensemble changes. This module repairs the R77 runner-level rolling/state interface only; strategy/execution semantics are imported UNMODIFIED from scripts/opencode_r77_advisor_core.py. No R77/core edits in this round (roll-wrapper fix only).

timeliness_policy.stale_after_description: signals older than 24 closed 5-minute bars (2h) past their decision bar are DIAGNOSTIC-only, never actionable alerts/intents
timeliness_policy.rationale: Pre-specified BEFORE implementation (unchanged from r78). N-decay ladder evidence (round10 v40: edge survives to d24/2h at +89%, dead at d48/4h) bounds the honest actionability horizon at (2h,4h]; 24 bars is the conservative end. NOTE (r79, kept in r80): this 24-bar rule is an OUTER bound only. It does NOT authorize retroactive next-bar execution on historical bars; the missed-clock rule below binds first.
timeliness_policy.enforcement: decision_time more than stale_after_bars*bar_seconds behind the current observation instant forces DIAGNOSTIC-only (gates untouched). Missed-clock (decision bar precedes the latest new bar of the ingest) forces DIAGNOSTIC-only independently of age.

missed_clock_policy.rule: Only decisions ON the latest new bar of an ingest may be actionable. Every earlier catch-up decision is DIAGNOSTIC-only: its entry window (signal_bar+1 onward) already passed before the decision actually became available, so simulating a fill is backtest fiction.
missed_clock_policy.choice: diagnostic-only. NO separately-versioned delayed-entry policy is shipped in r80.
missed_clock_policy.rationale: A late-placed limit order is a different execution (different queue position, different available prices) from the original next-bar entry; without a delayed-entry execution model versioned and shared with its batch reference, the only honest handling is diagnostic-only. A 2h signal-age rule alone is insufficient: a 65-minute-old signal (leader r78 repro) is 'timely' yet its entry bar long passed. Latest-new-bar alone is likewise insufficient to authorize backdated entry on a stale/late feed: decision/observation/earliest-fill times are validated, and a missed next-bar entry stays diagnostic.
missed_clock_policy.preserved: Already-observed pending/open positions settle causally through catch-up bars (observe_bar with raw=None advances accounts); historical fills are never silently rewritten.

economic_clock.rule: Execution-bar indices are timestamp-stable origin-anchored 5-minute grid steps: exec_idx = round((open_time - origin_open) / 300s), where origin_open is the first valid settled open of the run. Same candle time -> same exec_idx across uninterrupted, chunked, duplicated, gapped/backfilled and restarted consumption of identical data. Pending expiry (signal+expiry), holding timeout (entry+holding), control-trace ordering and truncation windows therefore follow ACTUAL candle times. Fresh elapsed-time indices are NEVER allocated to satisfy monotonic asserts; pending is NEVER reset/re-armed to conceal divergence.
economic_clock.gapless_parity: For gapless in-order runs the anchor reproduces the old 0..N-1 counter exactly, so r79 gapless economics are bit-identical under r80.
economic_clock.resume_compat: Clean r79 states (no paused/uncommitted seen-keys, no unresolved gaps) resume under r80: origin is derived as min_seen_open - min_idx*300s, which reproduces their indices. r79 states WITH unresolved gap-pause flags carry time-unstable counter indices (post-gap bars consumed fresh indices; backfilled times would collide) and are REFUSED with an explicit message: start a new run or replay from the complete window. ROLL_STATE_VERSION is unchanged (r78_roll_state/1); origin_open_iso and missing_opens are optional keys with defaults.

reconcile.identity: market (symbol/interval) + open_time UTC; positional-index modulo FORBIDDEN
reconcile.clock: absolute 5m grid from open_time (open % 300s == 0 since epoch, close == open + 300s) for execution identity; 6h UTC grid from open_time via r77 core.on_grid for inference decisions (absolute grid, never positional)
reconcile.gap_policy: FAIL CLOSED with pause: a gap stays UNRESOLVED until EVERY expected valid closed candle between its (after, before) boundaries (enumerated on the absolute 5m grid) is present in the seen-valid set, or the run is explicitly censored/invalid. Partial, out-of-order and overlapping backfills, repeated pauses and multiple restarts preserve the missing set and positions. Every new row at/after the earliest unresolved gap boundary is PAUSED: zero economic settlement, zero actionable intents, no gate consumption; replay after verified backfill reuses the SAME timestamp-stable exec_idx (exactly-once, no duplicates). Missing bars are NEVER synthesized and positions are NEVER settled through unobserved price paths. The pause persists across ingests until backfill; both empty and open portfolios are covered.
reconcile.revision_policy: historical OHLC revision on an already-settled bar is recorded as a persistent revision event; the settled record is kept (no silent overwrite, no re-settlement). Additionally: any ingest carrying revisions forces the WHOLE ingest diagnostic-only, because the inference frame consumes the full window and revised bytes must not reach inference silently. The revision decision is persistent in exec_state.revisions + validity history; an ingest diagnostic marker alone never clears an unresolved gap nor rewrites an open position.
reconcile.forming_policy: bars with close_time > observed_at are forming and excluded from settlement AND from the inference frame
reconcile.nonfinite_policy: bars with non-finite OHLC/volume are rejected (INCOMPLETE), excluded from settlement AND from the inference frame; an ingest with non-finite rows or a market mismatch forces diagnostic-only (fail closed)
reconcile.invalid_policy: bars failing OHLC consistency (high>=low, high/low vs open/close, volume>=0, close>open), 5m grid alignment (open % 300s == 0), or close-time exactness (close == open + 300s), or carrying NaT/naive-unparseable timestamps, are INVALID: never marked seen/settled, never silently counted as settled (counted as invalid_dropped), excluded from settlement AND the inference frame; an ingest carrying invalid rows forces diagnostic-only (fail closed)
reconcile.invalid_recovery: restored (backfilled) data recovers by resuming with the complete window: missing keys settle as new rows in time order with timestamp-stable indices, paused bars replay with the SAME stable exec_idx, identity map prevents duplicates

bootstrap.rule: Fresh bootstrap observation starts at the ACTUAL observed_at (fetch instant). Every pre-observation inference is DIAGNOSTIC-only: zero actionable intents, fills, gate consumption, funding or account PnL from historical warmup. Warmup may prime read-only feature state only.
bootstrap.replay_note: Replay mode is rehearsal, not observation: a fresh replay ingest likewise starts at its observed_at, so historical bars never produce actionable intents there either.

raw_provenance.rule: Every ingest writes its own immutable snapshot raw_ingest_<UTC-ts>_<sha8>_g<gen>.parquet (never a write-once-shared file). Each commit associates EXACTLY the bytes consumed (sha256 + first_open/last_close/row_count). The append-only ingest_manifest.jsonl records per ingest: ingest_id, kind (bootstrap/resume, FRESH-OBSERVATION vs REHEARSAL-NOT-LIVE), observed_at, range, sha256, prev_sha256, generation (bootstrap/resume observation times + lineage).
raw_provenance.legacy: Pre-r79 out dirs may contain a write-once raw_candles.parquet; r79+ never writes it and never hashes it as the consumed bytes.

checkpoint.scheme: generation-counter + atomic rename (temp file + fsync + os.replace) + append-only JSONL journal + CURRENT pointer; exports rebuilt from journal without re-emitting
checkpoint.corrupt_policy: corrupt/truncated CURRENT or checkpoint fails clearly (names the file+generation) or recovers from the last verified generation; never resume on unverified bytes

identity_verification.rule: hash actual file BYTES on resume (never accept a declared hash when bytes differ); any change forces an explicit new run (refuse resume naming the field)
identity_verification.note: checkpoint/calibrator model bytes listed in the prespec are also hashed when present on disk; missing model files fail closed (no stub substitution in production paths)
